ex.ja: 会合は次の金曜日まで延期された。

en: All; every; qualifying a singular noun, indicating all examples of the thing so named seen as individual or separate items (compare every).
For one; apiece; per.
Individually; separately; used in a sentence with a plural subject to indicate that the action or state described by the verb applies to …
Every one/thing individually or one by one.
An individual item: the least quantitative unit in a grouping.

each.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-West Germanic *aiwgahwalīk
Old English ǣġhwelċ
Old English ǣlċ
Middle English ech
English each
From Middle English ech, eche, elche, ilch, from Old English ǣlċ, contraction of ǣġhwelċ. Comparable to aye + alike.
Compare Scots ilk, elk (“each, every”), Saterland Frisian älk (“each”), West Frisian elk, elts (“each”), Dutch elk (“each”), Low German elk, ellik (“each”), German Low German elk, elke (“each, every”), German jeglicher (“any”). By surface analysis, Old English ā + which.

ex.en: Each of the students has his own shoes.
ex.ja: 学生たちはめいめい個人用の上履き靴がある。

ex.en: Each member has to pay a membership fee.
ex.ja: 各会員は会費を払うべし。

ex.en: I will see you, each in your turn.
ex.ja: 皆に順番に会いましょう。

note.ja: 古英語 ǣlc ＝ ā（いつも）+ gelīc（同じ）。「それぞれの」。every と同系。

en: Lacking something; failing.
Without a condom being worn.
Not having, containing, characteristic of, etc.
Not doing or not having done something.
Someone or something lacking in something.

without.ety:
From Middle English withoute, withouten, from Old English wiþūtan (literally “against the outside of”). By surface analysis, with- + out. Compare Dutch buiten (“outside of, without”), Danish uden (“without”), Swedish utan (“without”), Norwegian uten (“without”).
Superseded non-native Middle English sauns, sans (“without”), from Old French sans, sanz, senz (“without”).
Compare typologically Proto-Slavic *bez (“without”) (<+ Proto-Indo-European *h₁éǵʰs (“out”)).

ex.en: My life would be completely empty without you.
ex.ja: 君がいなければ私の人生は全くむなしいだろう。

ex.en: You shouldn't read people's private letters without permission.
ex.ja: 許可なしで他人の私的な手紙を読むべきではない。

ex.en: The train will arrive on time without fail.
ex.ja: 汽車は間違いなく定刻に到着いたします。

note.ja: with（〜と共に）+ out（外に）。「〜の外に」→「〜なしで」。

en: In a contrary direction to.
In physical opposition to; in collision with.

against.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *h₁én
Proto-Germanic *in
Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰengʰ-der.
Proto-Germanic *ganganąder.?
Proto-Germanic *gagin
Proto-Germanic *in gagin
Proto-West Germanic *in gagin
Old English onġēander.
Middle English ayenes
English against
Formed from Middle English ayenes, agenes, againes (“in opposition to”), a southern variant of agen, or directly from again, either way with adverbial genitive singular ending -es; the parasitic -t was added circa 1350, probably by confusion with the superlative ending -est. By surface analysis, again + -st (excrescent ending).
Cognate wi

ex.en: Are you for the war or against it?
ex.ja: 君は戦争に賛成か反対か。

ex.en: Flying against a strong wind is very difficult.
ex.ja: 強風に逆らって飛ぶのは大変なことだ。

ex.en: Not all the students are against the plan.
ex.ja: 学生の全員が計画に反対しているわけではない。

note.ja: again（向かい合って）+ -st。「向かい合って」→「〜に対して・反対して」→「〜にもたれて」。

en: The terminal point of something in space or time.
Share of joint responsibility.
To come to an end.
To conclude; to bring something to an end.

end.ety:
From Middle English ende, from Old English ende, from Proto-West Germanic *andī, from Proto-Germanic *andijaz (“end”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂entíos (“forehead; front”), from *h₂ent- (“face; forehead; front”), from *h₂en- (“on, onto”).
Cognates
Cognate with Yola een, eene (“end”), Saterland Frisian Eend, Eende (“end”), West Frisian ein (“end”), Alemannic German End, Endi (“end”), Central Franconian Eng, Enk (“end”), Cimbrian énte (“end”), Dutch eind, einde, end (“end”), German Ende (“end”), Luxembourgish Enn (“end”), Vilamovian end, ent (“end”), Danish, Norwegian Bokmål, and Norwegian Nyn

ex.en: The meeting ended at three in the afternoon.
ex.ja: 会合は午後３時に終わった。

ex.en: We came to an agreement in the end.
ex.ja: 我々はついに合意に達した。

ex.en: The movie "Fight Club" has a surprise ending.
ex.ja: 映画「ファイトクラブ」のエンディングには驚かされた。

note.ja: 核のイメージは「端・終わり」。終わり、端（the end of the road）、目的（a means to an end ＝ 目指す端）。

ja: 創立する（find の過去形・過去分詞でもある）

en: Food and lodging; board.
To start (an institution or organization).
To begin building.

ex.en: Where was it that you found this key?
ex.ja: 君がこのかぎを見つけたのはどこでしたか。

ex.en: On his return he found her daughter asleep.
ex.ja: 帰ってきた時、彼は娘が寝ているのを知った。

ex.en: We found that we had lost our way.
ex.ja: 我々は道に迷った事を知った。

note.ja: ラテン語 fundare（基礎を置く）から。fundus（底）。「土台を据える」→「設立する」。foundation、fundamental と同じ。find の過去形 found は別語。

en: To do as a requirement; indicates that the sentence subject is required as an imperative or directive to execute the sentence predicate, …
To do with certainty; indicates that the speaker is certain that the subject will have executed the predicate.
Something that is mandatory, required or recommended.

must.ety: From Middle English moste ("must", literally, "had to", the past tense of Middle English moten (“to have to”)), from Old English mōste (“had to”), 1st & 3rd person singular past tense of mōtan (“to be allowed, be able to, have the opportunity to, be compelled to, must, may”), from Proto-Germanic *mōtaną. Cognate with Dutch moest (“had to”), German musste (“had to”), Swedish måste (“must, have to, be obliged to”). More at mote.

ex.en: You must not look upon him as great.
ex.ja: 君は彼を偉大だとおもってはならない。

ex.en: You must know you're faced with a crisis.
ex.ja: 君は危機に直面していることを知らねばならんよ。

ex.en: You must state the fact as it is.
ex.ja: 君はその事実をありのまま述べなければならない。

note.ja: 古英語 mōste（〜してもよかった）から。意味が変わって「〜しなければならない」。

en: To display, convey or exhibit; to have something available for others to see; to direct attention to something.
To indicate; to convey facts that lead to a conclusion.
A play, dance, or other entertainment.
An exhibition of items.

show.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *(s)kewh₁-der.
Proto-Germanic *skawwōną
Proto-West Germanic *skauwōn
Old English scēawian
Middle English schewen
English show
From Middle English schewen, from Old English scēawian (“to look, look at, exhibit, display”), from Proto-West Germanic *skauwōn, from Proto-Germanic *skawwōną (“to look, see”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)kewh₁- (“to heed, look, feel, take note of”); see haw, gaum, caveat, caution.
Cognate with Scots shaw (“to show”), Dutch schouwen (“to inspect, view”), German schauen (“to see, behold”), Danish skue (“to behold”). Related to sheen.

ex.en: Show me a fact which supports your idea.
ex.ja: 君の考えを立証する事実をあげてほしい。

ex.en: I will show you how to solve it.
ex.ja: 解き方を教えてあげるよ。

ex.en: Please show me the way to the station.
ex.ja: 駅へ行く道を教えてください。

note.ja: 核のイメージは「見えるようにする」。見せる（show a ticket）、示す（show the way）、番組・ショー（見せるもの）、姿を見せる（show up）。

en: Of great size, large.
Fat.
In a loud manner.
In a boasting manner.
Someone or something that is large in stature.
An important or powerful person; a celebrity; a big name.

big.ety:
Inherited from Northern Middle English big, bigge (“powerful, strong”), possibly from a dialect of Old Norse. Ultimately perhaps a derivative of Proto-Germanic *bugja- (“swollen up, thick”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰew-, *bu- (“to swell”), in which case big would be related to bogey, bugbear, and bug.
Compare dialectal Norwegian bugge (“great man”), Low German Bögge, Boggelmann.

ex.en: When we are small, everything seems so big.
ex.ja: 子供の頃は、周りのものが何でも大きく見えるものだ。

ex.en: There was a big fire in my neighborhood.
ex.ja: 近所に大火事がありました。

ex.en: Mary spread the big map on the table.
ex.ja: メアリーは机の上に大きな地図を広げた。

note.ja: 中英語 big（強い）から。北欧語に由来するとされる。「大きい」→「重要な」。

en: To become aware of through the skin; to use the sense of touch on.
To find one's way (literally or figuratively) by touching or using cautious movements.
A perception experienced mainly or solely through the sense of touch.
A vague mental impression.

feel.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-West Germanic *fōlijan
Old English fēlan
Middle English felen
English feel
From Middle English felen, from Old English fēlan, from Proto-West Germanic *fōlijan.
Cognate with Dutch voelen and German fühlen.

ex.en: "I feel like playing cards." "So do I."
ex.ja: 「トランプしたいなあ」「私も」

ex.en: Not feeling well, I stayed home all day.
ex.ja: 気分が良くなかったの、１日中家にいた。

ex.en: When I came home, I felt very hungry.
ex.ja: 家に帰った時、とてもおなかがすいていた。

note.ja: 核のイメージは「体や心で感じる」。触って感じる（feel the cloth）、気分（feel happy）、思う（I feel that 〜）。

en: Physically secure and certain, non-failing, reliable.
Certain in one's knowledge or belief.
Without doubt, certainly.
Yes; of course.
Yes; I guess; you could say that; a weak or noncommittal positive response.

sure.ety:
From Middle English sure, seur, sur, from Middle French sur or Old French seür, from Latin sēcūrus (“secure”, literally “carefree”), from sē- (“apart”) + cūra (“care”) (compare Old English orsorg (“carefree”), from or- (“without”) + sorg (“care”)). See cure. Doublet of secure and the now obsolete or dialectal sicker (“certain, safe”).
Displaced native Middle English wis, iwis (“certain, sure”) (from Old English ġewis, ġewiss (“certain, sure”)), as well as Middle English siker (“sure, secure”) (from Old English sicor (“secure, sure”)) with which it was cognate.

ex.en: I'm sure your efforts will result in success.
ex.ja: 君の努力はきっと成功をおさめるだろう。

ex.en: Be sure to drop in at my house.
ex.ja: 必ず私の家に立ち寄りなさい。

ex.en: Why are you so sure of his success?
ex.ja: なぜ彼が成功すると確信がもてるの？

note.ja: ラテン語 securus（心配のない）から。secure と同じ語源。「確かな・確信している」、返事の「もちろん」。

en: A set of draught animals, such as two horses in front of a carriage.
Any group of people involved in the same activity, especially sports or work.
To form a group, as for sports or work.
To go together well; to harmonize.
Used to propose that another player team up with the speaker.

team.ety: From Middle English tem, teem, teme, from Old English tēam (“child-bearing, offspring, brood, set of draught animals”), from Proto-West Germanic *taum, from Proto-Germanic *taumaz (“that which draws or pulls”), from Proto-Germanic *taugijaną, *tugōną, *teuhōną, *teuhaną (“to lead, bring, pull, draw”), from Proto-Indo-European *dewk- (“to pull, lead”). Cognate with Scots team, teem (“a chain, harness”), Saterland Frisian Toom (“bridle; breeding”), West Frisian team (“bridle, team”), Dutch toom (“bridle, reins, flock of birds”), German Low German Toom (“bridle”), German Zaum (“bridle”), Danish t

ex.en: I'm glad that your team won the game.
ex.ja: 君のチームが試合に勝ってうれしい。

ex.en: Tom is the captain of this baseball team.
ex.ja: トムはこの野球チームのキャプテンだ。

ex.en: There is no knowing which team will win.
ex.ja: どちらのチームが勝つかわからない。

note.ja: 古英語 tēam（一組の家畜・子孫）から。teem（たくさんいる）と同系。「くびきでつながれた牛馬」→「チーム」。

en: Continuously, constantly, all the time (for the complete duration).
At any time.
Occurring at any time, occurring even but once during a timespan.

ever.ety:
From Middle English ever, from Old English ǣfre, originally a phrase whose first element undoubtedly consists of Old English ā (“ever, always”) + in (“in”) + an element possibly from feorh (“life, existence”) (dative fēore). Compare Old English ā tō fēore (“ever in life”), Old English feorhlīf (“life”) from feorh (“life”) + līf (“life”).
Sense 5 of the adverb was likely formed by association with never, which also carries the meaning of did not in colloquial Singaporean and Malaysian English. Also, compare Chinese 有 … 過 /有 … 过 (yǒu ... guò / jau⁵ ... gwo³, “has […] before”).

ex.en: Did you ever hear the like of it?
ex.ja: 君はそのようなことを聞いたことがあるか。

ex.en: Have you ever thought of becoming a nurse?
ex.ja: 看護婦になろうと考えたことはありますか。

ex.en: Did you ever make a speech in English?
ex.ja: 英語のスピーチをしたことがありますか。

note.ja: 古英語 ǣfre（いつも）から。「いつでも」→（疑問文で）「これまでに」。never、every と同じ。

en: A group of people who are closely related to one another (by blood, marriage or adoption); kin; in particular, a set of parents and their…
A group of related animals, usually a mother and offspring, a mating pair or larger lineages in some species.
Suitable for children and adults.

family.ety: From Late Middle English famylye, from Latin familia (“a household”). Displaced native Old English hīred and hād. Doublet of familia.

ex.en: We are expecting an addition to our family.
ex.ja: 我が家はもう一人増えそうです。

ex.en: The whole family set off on the trip.
ex.ja: 家族全員が旅行にでかけた。

ex.en: The whole family got out of the car.
ex.ja: 家族は全員車から降りた。

note.ja: ラテン語 familia（一家・召使いを含む家の者）から。→「家族・一族・（生物分類の）科」。familiar（家族のような→なじみのある）も同じ。

en: To continue in (a course or mode of action); to not intermit or fall from; to uphold or maintain.
To remain faithful to a given promise or word.
The main tower of a castle or fortress, located within the castle walls.
The food or money required to keep someone alive and healthy; one's support, maintenance.

keep.ety:
From Middle English kepen (“to keep, guard, look after, watch”), from Old English cēpan (“to seize, hold, observe”), from Proto-West Germanic *kōpijan, from Proto-Germanic *kōpijaną (“to look, heed, watch, observe”) (compare West Frisian kypje (“to look”)), from Proto-Indo-European *ǵab-, *ǵāb- (“to look after”) (compare Lithuanian žẽbti (“to eat reluctantly”), Russian забо́та (zabóta, “care, worry”)).
The dialectal sense of the verb meaning “to put back” or “put away” may be analyzed as a semantic loan from a local language—compare Welsh cadw and Mandarin 收 (shōu).

ex.en: I don't have the strength to keep trying.
ex.ja: 私にはやり続けるだけの強さがない。

ex.en: You had better not keep company with him.
ex.ja: 君は彼と交際しない方がよい。

ex.en: You can trust him to keep his word.
ex.ja: 君は彼が約束を守ると信じてよい。

note.ja: 核のイメージは「ある状態をずっと保つ」。持ち続ける（keep a diary）、状態を保つ（keep quiet）、続ける（keep running）、守る（keep a promise）。

en: Power, strength, force, or influence held by a person or group.
Physical strength or force.
Used to indicate a desired past action that was not done.
Used to indicate conditional or possible actions; would perhaps/maybe.

might.ety:
From Middle English maught, might, miȝt, myght, from Old English maht, meaht, meht, mieht, miht, mæht (“ability, power; strength; virtue”), from Proto-West Germanic *mahti, from Proto-Germanic *mahtiz (“ability, power; force, strength”), from Proto-Indo-European *(me)mógʰe (“to be able to, to have power”), from *megʰ- (“to be able”), corresponding to Germanic *maganą (“to be able, may”) + *-þiz. Equivalent to may + -th.
Cognates
Cognate with Scots micht (“might”), Yola mought (“might”), Dutch macht (“might, power”), German Macht (“might, power”), Luxembourgish Muecht (“authority, might, power”

ex.en: We were worried we might miss the train.
ex.ja: 我々は列車に遅れないかと心配だった。

ex.en: She might not know that we are here.
ex.ja: ひょっとすると彼女は私たちがここにいることを知らないのかもしれない。

ex.en: Why might he have done that, I wonder?
ex.ja: どうして彼はそんな事をしたのだろう。

note.ja: may の過去形。古英語 meahte。名詞の might（力）も同じ語根。「〜かもしれない」。

en: To make happy or satisfy; to give pleasure to.
To desire; to will; to be pleased by.
Used to make a polite request.
Used as an affirmative to an offer.
An expression of annoyance, impatience, or exasperation.

please.ety: From Middle English plesen, plaisen, borrowed from Old French plaise, conjugated form of plaisir or plaire, from Latin placeō (“to please, to seem good”), from the Proto-Indo-European *pleHk- (“pleasingness, permission”). In this sense, displaced native Old English līcian, whence Modern English like.

ex.en: "Pass me the salt, please." "Here you are."
ex.ja: 「塩を取って下さい」「はい、どうぞ」

ex.en: I am far from pleased with your behavior.
ex.ja: 君の振る舞いにはぜんぜん感心しない。

ex.en: Please remove your shoes before entering the house.
ex.ja: 靴を脱いでから家には入ってください。

note.ja: 古フランス語 plaisir（喜ばせる）から。ラテン語 placere。「（もし）あなたを喜ばせるなら」→「どうぞ」。pleasure、pleasant と同じ。

en: To physically place (something or somebody, in, at, around, etc. someplace)
To place in abstract; to attach or attribute; to assign.
The act of putting; an action; a movement; a thrust; a push.
An old card game.

put.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Germanic *putōną
Proto-West Germanic *putōn
Old English putian
Middle English putten
English put
From Middle English putten, pitten, pytten, puten, poten, from Old English putian, *pūtian ("to push, put out"; attested by derivative putung (“pushing, impulse, instigation, urging”)) and potian (“to push, thrust, strike, butt, goad”), both from Proto-West Germanic *putōn, from Proto-Germanic *putōną (“to stick, stab”), which is of uncertain origin. Possibly from Proto-Indo-European *bud- (“to shoot, sprout”), which would make it cognate with Sanskrit बुन्द (bundá, “arrow”), L

ex.en: I put on a little weight last year.
ex.ja: 去年少し体重が増えました。

ex.en: The meeting was put off until next Friday.
ex.ja: 会合は次の金曜日まで延期された。

ex.en: Circumstances forced us to put off the meeting.
ex.ja: 我々はやむを得ない事情で、その会合を延期した。

note.ja: 核のイメージは「ある場所に置く」。物を置く（put a book on the desk）から、言葉にする（put it simply ＝ 言葉の中に置く）、状態に置く（put him at ease）へ。

en: A generally accepted means of exchange.
A currency maintained by a state or other entity which can guarantee its value (such as a monetary union).

money.ety:
Etymology tree
Latin Monēta
Latin monēta
Old French moneie
Old French monoie
Anglo-Norman muneiebor.
Middle English moneye
English money
From Middle English moneye, moneie, money, borrowed from Anglo-Norman muneie (“money”), from Latin monēta (“money, a place for coining money, coin, mint”), from the name of the temple of Juno Moneta in Rome, where a mint was.
In this sense, displaced native Old English feoh, whence English fee. Doublet of mint, ultimately from the same Latin word but through Germanic and Old English, and of manat, through Russian and Azerbaijani or Turkmen.

ex.en: Why did you use up all the money?
ex.ja: 君はなぜお金を使い果たしたのか。

ex.en: Thanks to you, I spent all my money.
ex.ja: 君のおかげで、全財産を使っちゃったよ。

ex.en: How much money did you spend in total?
ex.ja: 使った金額は全部で幾らですか？

note.ja: ラテン語 moneta から。ローマで貨幣を鋳造したユノ・モネタ（「警告する者」の意、monere）の神殿に由来する。→「お金」。monitor（警告する人→監視する）と同じ mon。

en: Unconstrained.
Not imprisoned or enslaved.
Without needing to pay.
To make free; set at liberty; release.
To rid of something that confines or oppresses.
A free transfer.
The usual means of restarting play after a foul is committed, where the non-offending team restarts from where the foul was committed.

free.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *preyH-
Proto-Indo-European *-ós
Proto-Indo-European *priHós
Proto-Germanic *frijwaz
Proto-West Germanic *friu
Old English frēo
Middle English fre
English free
From Middle English fre, from Old English frēo, frēoh, frī, friġ, frīoh (“free”), from Proto-West Germanic *frī, from Proto-Germanic *frijaz (“beloved, not in bondage”), from Proto-Indo-European *priHós (“pleased, loved”), from *preyH- (“to please; to love”). Related to friend.
cognates, etc
Germanic cognates include Scots fre (“free”), North Frisian frai, frei, fri, Frii (“free”), Saterland Frisian fr

ex.en: If you are free, give me a hand.
ex.ja: 暇だったら、手伝ってください。

ex.en: Every student has free access to the library.
ex.ja: 学生はだれでも自由に図書館を利用できる。

ex.en: What do you do in your free time?
ex.ja: 暇なときは何をしていますか。

note.ja: 核のイメージは「束縛がない」。自由な、無料の（free of charge ＝ 料金から自由）、暇な（free time）、〜がない（sugar-free）。

en: Number-two; following after the first one with nothing between them. The ordinal number corresponding to the cardinal number two.
Next to the first in value, power, excellence, dignity, or rank; secondary; subordinate; inferior.
After the first; at the second rank.
After the first occurrence but before the third.
Something that is number two in a series.
Something that is next in rank, quality, precedence, position, status, or authority.
To agree as a second person to (a proposal), usually to reach a necessary quorum of two. (See etymology 3 for translations.)
To follow in the next place; to succeed.

second.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *sekʷ-der.
Proto-Italic *sekʷondo-
Latin secunduslbor.
Old French secondbor.
Middle English secunde
English second
From Middle English secunde, second, secound, secund, borrowed from Old French second, seond, from Latin secundus (“following, next in order”), from root of sequor (“to follow”), from Proto-Indo-European *sekʷ- (“to follow”). Doublet of secund and secundo. Displaced native twoth and partially displaced native other (from Old English ōþer (“other; next; second”)).

ex.en: You are telling it second hand, aren't you?
ex.ja: それは受け売りだろう？

ex.en: It is at best a second-rate hotel.
ex.ja: それはせいぜい二流のホテルだ。

ex.en: Mrs. Smith gave birth to her second child.
ex.ja: スミス夫人には二番目の子供が生まれた。

note.ja: ラテン語 secundus（次に続く）から。sequi（続く）の仲間。→「2番目の」、時間を2回目に細かく分けた単位 →「秒」。

en: One or some person of unspecified or indefinite identity.
A partially specified but unnamed person.
An important person.

someone.ety: From Middle English sum on, sum one, sum oon, equivalent to some + one.

ex.ja: 君の代行者を見つけよう。

ex.en: I heard someone calling me from a distance.
ex.ja: 遠くから誰かが私に呼びかけているのが聞こえた。

ex.en: Bob was looking for someone to talk with.
ex.ja: ボブは誰か話し相手を探していた。

en: From a place, hence.
Aside; off; in another direction.
Away with you! Go away! Begone!
Not here, gone, absent, unavailable, traveling; on vacation.
At a specified distance in space, time, or figuratively.
To depart; to go to another place.

away.ety:
From Middle English away, awey, awei, oway, o wey, on way, from Old English āweġ, onweġ (“away”), originally on weġ (“on one's way; onward; on”), equivalent to a- (“on”) + way.
Cognate with Scots awa, away (“away”), Old Frisian aweg, awei (“away”), Saterland Frisian wäch, wääge (“away”), Dutch weg (“away”), German weg (“away”), Danish væk (“away”), Swedish i väg (“away; off; along”).

ex.ja: 危険な状態にあるとき、彼らは逃げます。

ex.en: We should do away with the death penalty.
ex.ja: 我々は死刑を廃止すべきである。

ex.en: My family will be away for a week.
ex.ja: 家族で一週間留守にします。

note.ja: 古英語 onweg ＝ on（〜に）+ way（道）。「道に出て」→「離れて」。

On the left side.
Towards the left side.
The left side or direction.
The left-wing political parties as a group; citizens holding left-wing views as a group.

ex.ja: 君が戻るまえに私は出かけてしまっているだろう。

ex.en: There's a lot of room left for improvement.
ex.ja: 改善の余地は大いに残されている。

ex.en: The weather was lovely when I left home.
ex.ja: 家を出る時には晴れていました。

note.ja: 古英語 lyft（弱い）から。利き手でない弱い方の手 →「左」。政治の「左派」はフランス革命の議会の席から。leave の過去形 left は別語。

en: Quantity of countable things.
An abstract entity used to describe quantity.
To total or count; to amount to.
To limit to a certain number; to reckon (as by fate) to be few in number.

A settlement granted special status by royal charter or letters patent; traditionally, a settlement with a cathedral regardless of size.

A separate, appropriated portion; a quantized, subdivided set consisting a whole.

ex.ja: 君の英語はとても上達したと思う。

ex.en: We had a lot of snow last year.
ex.ja: 去年は雪が多かった。

en: Any nounal word or phrase which indicates a particular person, place, class, or thing.
A reputation.
To give a name to.
To mention, specify.

The period of darkness beginning at the end of evening astronomical twilight when the sun is 18 degrees below the horizon, and ending at …
To spend a night (in a place), to overnight.

ex.ja: 我々はしゃべりづめで夜半まで起きていた。

Activity for amusement only, especially among the young.
Similar activity in young animals, as they explore their environment and learn new skills.

en: Up to the time of (something happening); pending.
Up to (a certain place)
Up to the time that (a condition becomes true).
Before (a condition becoming true).

ex.ja: 君たちは彼らが到着するまで出発しないほうがいいよ。

ex.ja: 教会に着くまでまっすぐ行きなさい。

ex.en: The meeting was put off until next Friday.
ex.ja: 会合は次の金曜日まで延期された。

note.ja: 北欧語 und（〜まで）+ till（〜まで）。till と同じ意味を重ねた語。

en: A team; a group of people who work together for a common purpose.
A group of performing artists who put on shows together.

Displaced native Old English werod, gefer, getæl, and hired.

ex.ja: 君は彼と交際しない方がよい。

ex.ja: 会社は彼の転勤願いを却下した。

ex.en: You have, no doubt, heard of our company.
ex.ja: あなたは弊社のことを既にご存じかと思います。

note.ja: com（共に）+ pan（パン）+ y。一緒にパンを食べる仲間 →「仲間・同席」→「会社」。companion（仲間）も同じ。

en: An indefinite, but usually small, number of.
Not many; a small (in comparison with another number stated or implied) but somewhat indefinite number of.
Few people, few things.

From Middle English fewe, from Old English fēaw (“few”), from Proto-West Germanic *fau, from Proto-Germanic *fawaz (“few”), from Proto-Indo-European *peh₂w- (“few, small”).

ex.en: Could you give me a few more minutes?
ex.ja: もう少し待ってください。

To allow to be or do without interference; to not disturb or meddle with; to leave alone.
The allowing of possession of a property etc. in exchange for rent.

en: True, genuine, not merely nominal or apparent.
Genuine, not artificial, counterfeit, or fake.
Really; very.
A commodity; see realty.
One of the three genders that the common gender can be separated into in the Scandinavian languages.

ex.ja: 彼は本当の自分をしらないようだ。

In contrast.
But, yet, though, although.
